_why_this_file_exists: The Gate 4N-I3 closure test iterated the same Python dict that generated the policy, so a defect in that dict changed both the policy and its expected value simultaneously — the test could not fail. This file is a SEPARATE SOURCE, authored from evidence rather than generated. scripts/gen_operator_policies.py MUST NOT read or write it, and tests/test_operator_policies.py compares the generated policy AGAINST it.

stage_a_create_closure._scope: module.revision_reader Stage A only: publication_bootstrap_enabled = true, runtime_enabled = false.
stage_a_create_closure._ordering_hazard: OpenTofu creates the two ECR resources before the IAM role. If the IAM grant cannot match, the apply fails AFTER the ECR resources already exist — a partial apply. This is why the boundary precondition must be asserted BEFORE apply, not discovered during it.
stage_a_create_closure._boundary_dependency: aws_iam_role.reader_publisher sets permissions_boundary = var.role_permissions_boundary_arn. If that variable is null the provider sends no boundary, so a CreateRole grant conditioned on iam:PermissionsBoundary can never match. Stage A therefore REQUIRES the variable to be set to the exact boundary ARN and the boundary policy to exist.
stage_a_create_closure._ecr_read_note: ecr:GetRepositoryPolicy was in an earlier draft of this contract and is REMOVED: it has never been called by this principal, and provider v6.55.0 internal/service/ecr/repository.go reads exclusively via findRepositoryByName -> DescribeRepositories. Removing it is a correction to THIS FILE, caught by the independence test comparing contract against generated policy.
stage_a_create_closure._ecr_create_note: PutImageScanningConfiguration and PutImageTagMutability are granted DEFENSIVELY. On a fresh create the provider passes imageScanningConfiguration and imageTagMutability as CreateRepository parameters, so they are not strictly needed; but repository.go exposes both as UPDATE calls, and the reader repository sets image_tag_mutability=IMMUTABLE and scan_on_push=true (modules/revision_reader/main.tf:68-75). If the repository already exists with different settings, the apply would call them and fail mid-run. Given Defect 5 was a mid-apply failure after partial creation, the defensive grant is the correct trade.
stage_a_create_closure._iam_list_role_tags_note: iam:ListRoleTags is required on the CREATE path only. Provider v6.55.0 internal/service/iam/role.go defines roleTags() calling ListRoleTags via a paginator. It was NOT observed during the reference refresh, but that refresh only read ALREADY-EXISTING roles; no reader role has ever been created, so absence there proves nothing about the create path. Granted to the temporary operator, withheld from permanent W0.
stage_a_create_closure._gate_4n_i9_note: iam_create was REMOVED from this section in Gate 4N-I9 and moved to role_bootstrap_closure. Stage-A now consumes PRE-EXISTING roles and holds no role authoring capability of any kind.

state_backend_closure._note: Required by tofu init/plan/apply against the S3 backend. Held by the temporary operator AND — since INFRA-9 B-3 (2026-08-16) — by permanent W0, which the Stage-A barrier established as the apply identity. In both principals every capability is scoped to the exact backend resource and re-denied everywhere else by a NotResource fence; W0 additionally conditions the CMK use on kms:ViaService (s3/dynamodb) so the state blob cannot be decrypted by a direct KMS call.
state_backend_closure._lock_note: dynamodb:DescribeTable was PROVEN UNUSED by the OpenTofu 1.12.5 S3 backend: every DescribeTable on the lock table came from aws-cli, resource-explorer, or BootstrapOp managing the table. Excluded.
state_backend_closure._cmk_note: GenerateDataKey and Decrypt are PROVEN REQUIRED: the state bucket has BucketKeyEnabled and the lock table is encrypted with the SAME CMK, with CloudTrail showing both encryption contexts. kms:Encrypt was never observed and is excluded.
state_backend_closure._use_lockfile_hazard: RESOLVED (INFRA-9 B-3 Part A, 2026-08-16). The operator-held backend config was read in-process during the Part-A adjudication: use_lockfile is NOT set, so locking is DynamoDB-only and no <key>.tflock object operations exist. s3:DeleteObject stays excluded. If an operator ever enables use_lockfile, this closure is WRONG until re-adjudicated — the hazard text above is retained so that condition is checked, not assumed.

stage_b_task_definition_closure._scope: INFRA-9 B-3 apply-identity delta (2026-08-16): task-definition registration by permanent W0, the apply identity. NO task definition is registered in the Stage-A apply at all (corrected per permissions-lane round-2 N2): module.revision_reader gates its task resource on runtime_enabled AND publication_bootstrap_enabled AND a pinned image digest (create_task in modules/revision_reader/task.tf), and runtime_enabled is STAGE B; the api/worker/migration families (module ecs, deploy_workload) are likewise Stage B. The correction STRENGTHENS the exposure-bounding argument in _no_passrole_note — a full stage of runway exists before the pre-flight gate must fire, and the gate is due before STAGE-B RUNTIME ENABLEMENT.
stage_b_task_definition_closure._register_note: Resource-scoped to the four composition family ARNs in the family:* form ONLY. Evidence (retained at b3-part-a-live-readback/ecs-action-truth-evidence.md): the Service Reference lists Resources=[task-definition] for RegisterTaskDefinition with a REVISION-BEARING ARNFormats entry, and this account's own CloudTrail AccessDenied of 2026-07-28T01:38:31Z names the authorization resource as task-definition/<family>:* — a bare-family entry never matches and was removed as dead weight. ecs:TagResource travels with registration because every composition task definition is registered WITH tags and ECS tag-on-create performs an additional ecs:TagResource authorization (six-lane permissions-lane finding 3; the same defensive-grant reasoning as _ecr_create_note). aws:RequestTag/aws:TagKeys/ecs:task-cpu/ecs:task-memory/privileged condition keys are supported and deliberately NOT used: their values are module-variable-owned and a wrong literal deadens the grant exactly when it is needed; family scoping plus the role boundary and image-publication controls carry that risk instead.
stage_b_task_definition_closure._no_passrole_note: iam:PassRole is NOT granted, and whether RegisterTaskDefinition performs a PassRole authorization check when executionRoleArn/taskRoleArn are supplied is recorded as DISPUTED — not asserted in either direction (the iam_eval.DISPUTED_RUNTIME_CONTEXT posture). The ECS API Reference documents both parameters with no caller PassRole statement; general PassRole doctrine and AmazonECS_FullAccess's conditioned PassRole suggest it is expected somewhere in the workflow; and this account's ONLY successful registration (2026-07-28T02:44:33Z, db-bootstrap) ran WITH a temporary PassRole allow in force (batch4c5 records), so no observation settles it. Keeping zero PassRole surface is the fail-closed direction: if AWS enforces it, the apply fails with AccessDenied at the task-definition step, and the exposure is bounded because the composition registers task definitions only in a later digest-pinned apply. MANDATORY PART-B PRE-FLIGHT GATE: resolve the dispute BEFORE any apply that reaches a task definition. ONLY an authorized single CANARY REGISTRATION (or an authoritative AWS documentation statement) can settle it — iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy is EXPLICITLY INSUFFICIENT: it evaluates named actions against policies, cannot model whether ECS internally performs a PassRole authorization while servicing RegisterTaskDefinition, and does not evaluate SCPs; a green simulator run must never be recorded as satisfying this gate (permissions-lane round-2 N1). The canary must be registered WITH TAGS so the same probe also settles the ecs:TagResource tag-on-create authorization shape (round-2 N4). If PassRole proves required, the grant (exact role ARNs + iam:PassedToService=ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com + fence) is a SEPARATE reviewed delta.
stage_b_task_definition_closure._describe_note: Read-back after registration. AWS supports NO resource-level scoping for DescribeTaskDefinition (Service Reference, current: Resources=[]) -> Resource "*" with the aws:RequestedRegion condition, the same documented-limitation posture as rds:DescribeDBInstances. Recorded: at "*" this reads ANY task definition in the account, including plaintext environment blocks; this repo's definitions carry environment=[] and reference secrets by ARN only, and the grant must not be reused later as an ordinary read.
stage_b_task_definition_closure._verify_closure_limitation: provider-api-operation-map.json's aws_ecs_task_definition entry deliberately gains NO create axis: verify_closure checks create actions against the TEMPORARY operator, which correctly DENIES registration — the joiner has no model of the W0-versus-temporary ownership split for create actions. The ENTIRE task-definition surface sits outside the join, not just the create axis: the map entry is dark:true and verify_closure routes dark reads into deferred_dark, which is never checked against permanent W0, so ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition is outside the joiner too (permissions-lane round-2 N3). Both axes are therefore validated by this contract plus tests/test_operator_policies.py only; extending the joiner with per-principal create ownership is a recorded Part-B follow-up (six-lane architect-lane finding 6).
stage_b_task_definition_closure._excluded: ecs:DeregisterTaskDefinition is excluded: the delta covers create-only registration; revision replacement/retirement is a separate future adjudication. dynamodb:DescribeTable and kms:Encrypt — present in the LIVE 2026-07-27 policy — are excluded as proven unused by the OpenTofu 1.12.5 backend (DescribeTable is a management event, observable and never observed from the backend; kms:Encrypt per the S3 SSE-KMS model). dynamodb:UpdateItem is excluded on BACKEND-SOURCE grounds, not observation: DynamoDB data events are not on this trail, so absence of observation proves nothing — the S3 backend's lock client calls exactly GetItem, conditional PutItem and DeleteItem (six-lane permissions-lane finding 7).

ic_provisioning_closure._scope: INFRA-9 B-3 Part-B remediation (2026-08-17, OD-R1..OD-R5 adjudication): the ICPermAdmin provisioning delta — the capability Identity Center exercises WITH THE CALLER'S CREDENTIALS while servicing ProvisionPermissionSet for the W0 permission set. This section justifies the SINGLE statement scripts/gen_operator_policies.py emits as icpermadmin_provisioning_delta; it is NOT an operator requirement section and must never join the W0/temporary requirement joins in scripts/allow_model.py — the principal is ICPermAdmin, whose full permission-set document remains operator-held and outside this repository.
ic_provisioning_closure._denial_provenance: Two independent terminal-FAILED provisioning denials name exactly iam:PutRolePolicy performed by Identity Center with the caller's (ICPermAdmin session) credentials: B-1 (2026-08-13) and B-3 Part-B M2 (2026-08-17, request recorded in the operator evidence directory, part-b evidence record). The July 2026-07-27/28 provisioning writes SUCCEEDED attributed 'Root invokedBy sso.amazonaws.com' — in this account IC performs the reserved-role write as a forward-access call under the invoking session. Directed rollback R1 (2026-08-17) restored byte-identical permission-set/role parity before this remediation; effective live W0 permissions never changed during the blocked attempt.
ic_provisioning_closure._minimality: OD-R1: iam:PutRolePolicy is the ONLY action either denial ever named, and the only pending write in a W0 provisioning run — the reserved role already exists with a correct trust policy, exactly one inline policy, zero managed policies and no boundary (Part-B opening-gate parity proof). Every further IC-side requirement must surface as its own exact terminal-FAILED denial and be added by its own reviewed delta (deny-driven minimality).
ic_provisioning_closure._exact_role_scope: OD-R2: the Resource is the EXACT current W0 reserved-role ARN, supplied at generation time from the approved operator-held inputs (the live get-role read), validated against the anchor-resolved W0 permission-set name and a 16-lowercase-hex suffix, and bound by an operator-held sha256 pin. No suffix wildcard (it would silently cover a future role nobody reviewed), no reserved-path wildcard, no other programme role, and no ICPermAdmin self-scope (self-scope plus the existing PutInlinePolicyToPermissionSet capability would make ICPermAdmin fully self-modifying — a separately adjudicated trust decision, refused).
ic_provisioning_closure._condition_hypothesis: OD-R3: the statement requires StringEquals aws:CalledViaFirst = sso.amazonaws.com. SUPPORT is documented (the AWS FAS user guide states the CalledVia keys are populated with the initiating service principal when FAS requests are made — retained verbatim in the operator evidence directory, remediation-doc-evidence DOC-1); POPULATION on Identity Center's provisioning write is UNPROVEN and recorded in iam_eval.DISPUTED_RUNTIME_CONTEXT, and DOCUMENTATION remains DOCUMENTATION_INSUFFICIENT — this repository must never relabel that inference as documented proof. CORRECTION (supersedes the earlier claim that a SUCCEEDED provisioning status alone proves the condition): a terminal ProvisionPermissionSet status of SUCCEEDED does NOT by itself prove aws:CalledViaFirst was present or matched, because Identity Center may diff-and-skip the downstream iam:PutRolePolicy write when the reserved role already carries the target policy (the current parity state) — a SUCCEEDED status without an EXERCISED write proves nothing about the condition. CONDITION_LIVE therefore requires a CloudTrail iam:PutRolePolicy ALLOWED action-truth event bound to the expected probe submission, the expected caller/session context (userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer resolving to the ICPermAdmin reserved role, invokedBy=sso.amazonaws.com), the exact hashed target role, an appropriate event time, and the sole-grant premise (the materialized role carries exactly one iam:PutRolePolicy allow on that role — the conditioned statement — so an Allowed decision is attributable to it). CloudTrail lookup-events does NOT reveal the authorization-time aws:CalledViaFirst value, and invokedBy is NOT proof of condition-key population; the IAM policy simulator is EXPLICITLY INSUFFICIENT for service-to-service runtime population and must never be recorded as satisfying this gate. A SUCCEEDED request WITHOUT the required Allowed write event is INDETERMINATE_WRITE_NOT_EXERCISED, never CONDITION_LIVE. A single controlled denial may be classified PROVISIONAL_CONDITION_DEAD ONLY after BOTH discriminations pass: (a) explicit-deny discrimination — the denial is corroborated by a CloudTrail AccessDenied iam:PutRolePolicy action-truth event bound to the expected probe, the expected caller/session context and the exact hashed target role after the full ingestion dwell, and carries no explicit-deny indication; a denial attributable to an SCP, a permissions boundary, a session policy, or any other explicit deny routes to INDETERMINATE, never to condition-dead; and (b) sole-grant discrimination — the sole-grant premise holds at observation time (exactly one iam:PutRolePolicy allow on the target role — the conditioned statement — under a current, non-stale authorization plane, with the expected caller and the expected target), so the denial cannot be explained by a stale authorization plane, a wrong target, a wrong caller, or another grant; any such attribution routes to INDETERMINATE, never to condition-dead. Even a fully discriminated denial is only PROVISIONAL_CONDITION_DEAD — fail closed, no widening — and may NOT by itself authorize aws:ViaAWSService, condition removal, resource widening, or any additional IAM action. Any confirmation observation requires a SEPARATE authorization and a SEPARATE window; later observations are NON-UPGRADING (they cannot erase or replace the first result; disagreement is CONFLICTING_OBSERVATIONS and can never produce CONDITION_LIVE). No retry and no same-window disambiguation path exists. Any relaxation (e.g. aws:ViaAWSService) is a SEPARATE reviewed delta on proven non-population, never an in-place fallback.

_condition_liveness_evidence_standard._note: OD-R4 rev-3.1 correction, machine-checkable form of _condition_hypothesis. A terminal SUCCEEDED status is NOT proof of the condition; the CloudTrail Allowed action-truth event is. See the OD-R4 execution packet (operator evidence directory).
_condition_liveness_evidence_standard.condition_live_requires: CloudTrail iam:PutRolePolicy Allowed action-truth event bound to the probe submission, caller/session context, exact hashed target, event time, and the sole-grant premise

ic_provisioning_closure._permanent_assignment_invariant: OD-R2 pin: the W0 permission set MUST retain at least one standing account assignment. AWS documentation (retained DOC-2): deleting ALL assignments deletes the reserved role, and a later re-assignment mints a role with a DIFFERENT unique suffix — every exact-ARN reference goes stale. Because this delta pins the exact ARN, suffix rotation makes the grant DEAD (fails closed: provisioning simply denies again) and the ONLY path forward is a separately reviewed re-pin: a fresh operator-held ARN capture, a new sha256 pin, a re-generated delta and a repeat of the bootstrap provisioning step. Removing the last W0 assignment is therefore a reviewed governance event, never routine hygiene.
ic_provisioning_closure._bootstrap_circularity: The grant lands in ICPermAdmin's OWN permission-set document, but materializing it requires provisioning the ICPermAdmin reserved role — which IC performs with ICPermAdmin's credentials, needing exactly the capability being installed. The first provisioning is irreducibly out-of-band: the adjudicated direction (OD-R4, design only — NOT authorized by the repository change) is a one-time root-console permission-set DOCUMENT SAVE (the account-assignment 'reprovision' modal is excluded as the four-time API-invisible no-op surface; root CLI is excluded), gated on an API-visible provisioning request reaching SUCCEEDED. After that single step, all future W0 provisioning runs as CLI ProvisionPermissionSet under ICPermAdmin, and any future ICPermAdmin policy change repeats the bootstrap step (rare and deliberate — no self-scope).
ic_provisioning_closure._excluded: iam:CreateRole and iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy (first-provision to a NEW account: the role exists; role creation is a strictly larger capability), iam:AttachRolePolicy / iam:DetachRolePolicy (the W0 permission set carries zero managed policies by design), iam:DeleteRolePolicy (needed only if a permission-set policy is ever REMOVED — a different, unreviewed operation), iam:GetRole / iam:ListRolePolicies / iam:GetRolePolicy (read-only probes IC MAY make; deny-driven minimality withholds them until a denial names them — a FAILED provisioning run is proven recoverable, an over-grant is a standing capability). aws:ViaAWSService as the condition (broader: ANY forward-access service could exercise the write) is excluded per OD-R3 and requires a separate reviewed delta on proven non-population of aws:CalledViaFirst.
ic_provisioning_closure._fallback_posture: Hard stops, all fail-closed: a provisioning FAILED naming a NEW action -> retained denial, separate reviewed delta (OD-R1 path). The SAME iam:PutRolePolicy denial after the grant materialized -> condition-mismatch evidence ONLY after the _condition_hypothesis discriminations pass (a CloudTrail AccessDenied iam:PutRolePolicy action-truth event bound to the expected probe, caller/session context and exact hashed target, surviving explicit-deny and sole-grant discrimination — a denial attributable to an SCP, a permissions boundary, a session policy, a stale authorization plane, a wrong target, a wrong caller, or another grant is INDETERMINATE, never condition-dead); even then the classification is PROVISIONAL_CONDITION_DEAD and the only path is a separate reviewed delta (OD-R3 path), never an in-place widening. Suffix rotation -> dead grant, separately reviewed re-pin (_permanent_assignment_invariant). No live negative PutRolePolicy probes exist in this design (OD-R5: identical-byte writes still alter attribution and are mutation-class); enforcement is structural — the shape and mutation tests in tests/test_operator_policies.py — plus the mandatory positive artifact defined in _condition_hypothesis: the CloudTrail iam:PutRolePolicy Allowed action-truth event bound to an authorized probe under the sole-grant premise (the provisioning run itself, and a terminal SUCCEEDED status alone, are NOT the positive control — SUCCEEDED without the exercised write is INDETERMINATE_WRITE_NOT_EXERCISED).

role_bootstrap_closure._scope: GATE 4N-I9 DEFECT 1. iam:CreateRole accepts the AssumeRolePolicyDocument and AWS has no condition key over the whole trust document, so a principal holding it for an approved role NAME can still create that role with attacker-chosen trust that OUTLIVES the principal's expiry. These actions therefore no longer belong to the Stage-A operator; they belong to a separate, minimal RoleBootstrapOperator whose safety rests on exact reviewed trust files plus mandatory post-create read-back and immediate rollback on mismatch.
role_bootstrap_closure._enforcement_is_operational_not_iam: AWS offers no prevent here. The control is detect-and-revert, and it is recorded as such rather than described as if IAM enforced the trust bytes.
